title: Establish change-aware SLO muting and graded-response alert policy
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary:
Recent capacity regressions caused by an autoscaler misconfiguration produced high transient SLO burn that generated a storm of burn-rate pagers across multiple routes. On investigation we found that alerts are currently blind to cluster-change and deploy-change signals and therefore treat transient, expected burns the same as spontaneous regressions.

Goal:
Introduce a change-aware SLO muting layer and a graded-response alert policy so that: (1) alerts triggered within an identified change window (deploy, autoscaler scale events, model swap) are emitted at reduced severity (no immediate paging) and (2) alerts escalate if the burn persists beyond an explicit, measurable recovery window. This reduces page noise while preserving rapid escalation for genuine regressions.

Scope in this ticket:
- Define a canonical set of change signals we ingest (deploy events, cluster autoscaler events, model variant changes, region failover markers).
- Implement a muting policy engine in the monitoring pipeline to annotate burn-rate events with change context and apply a graded-response policy.
- Add Console controls for route-level muting sensitivity and a toggle for "change-aware alerting".
- Update runbooks and on-call docs.
- Add dashboards and SLO charts showing mitigated vs unmitigated burn counts for 90d backfill sampling.

Out of scope:
- Deep autoscaler fixes (ENG-21459) and exhaustive autoscaling rework; those are tracked separately.
- Major UI redesign beyond the small Console controls and docs links.
actions: Instrument event stream: ensure deploys, autoscaler scale events, and model-variant swaps are visible to the monitoring pipeline (owner: Infra Events)
Design policy semantics: define change-window durations (short: 5m, medium: 30m, long: 3h) and escalation thresholds per route tier (owner: Miguel)
Policy engine: add change-aware annotation and mute/soften logic to the burn-rate alert pipeline (owner: Observability Team)
Console controls: small UX surface to set default sensitivity per customer/tier and an override per route (owner: Console PM + Frontend)
Backfill and metrics: run a 90d backfill to estimate how many pagers would be suppressed and validate no regression misses (owner: Analytics)
Update runbooks: document expected behaviors and instructions for forcing escalation when needed (owner: SRE)
Canary rollout: enable for internal orgs, monitor for 72h, then enable progressively for low/high tiers (owner: Reliability)
Post-deploy review: capture metrics and adjust thresholds (owner: Miguel)
Follow-up: schedule a review with autoscaler owners to align on event semantics (owner: Asha)
acceptance_criteria: Monitoring pipeline annotates burn events with change context for deploys, autoscaler events, and model swaps
Burn-rate alerts created within a defined change-window are emitted as non-pager (ticket/comment) or INFO by default
If burn persists beyond the selected change-window the alert escalates to WARNING and then PAGE according to defined hysteresis rules
Console shows a route-level toggle and sensitivity slider; changing it updates policy behavior within 5 minutes
90-day backfill shows a reduction in pagers without >1 undetected sustained regression (operational false negative rate < 0.5%)
Runbook updated and on-call knows how to force-escalate or opt-out for an incident
Canary rollout executed and metrics collected: pager-rate, mean-time-to-detect (MTTD), mean-time-to-recover (MTTR) are within 10% of pre-change baselines for non-related regressions

2026-03-12 — Miguel Torres: Proposal for policy semantics uploaded to Confluence: short windows for hot restarts (5m), medium windows for deploy ramps (30m), long windows for region maintenance (3h). Seeking PM feedback on defaults.

2026-03-13 — PM Review (Lucas Meyer): Supportive of default sensitivity: internal orgs 30m, low-tier customers 15m, enterprise customers 5m with opt-out. Console toggle required for compliance use-cases.

2026-03-14 — Observability (Rina Kapoor): Implemented prototype that tags burn events with change.context and returns 'suppress' decisions for the prototype thresholds. PR: github.com/redwood/mon/PR/4122

notes:
Design trade-offs considered: (1) full muting vs graded-response — we chose graded-response to avoid silent failures; (2) short default windows risk noisy pages if events are missed — mitigated by requiring matching event IDs and soft-fallbacks; (3) legal/compliance opt-outs: enterprise customers can disable muting.

Follow-up tickets to create after initial rollout: create a dedicated autoscaler tagging RFC (owner: Infra), audit of past missed regressions (Analytics), and a possible enhancement to allow customer-driven SLA exemptions in the Console.
